## [0.0.9] - 2026-11-20

### Fixed

- **Every event `events_list` lists is kind `issue`, the one kind `linear.activity` declares.** A notification that
  names no issue was listed as kind `event`, which Memory refuses event by event, without storing them, while its
  cursor moves past them. It is kind `issue` now, and keeps its former kind as the label `event`. The declared
  `sources` are unchanged, so their descriptor hash is too.

### Known limits

- **Linear decides its tools.** The plugin's tool table follows Linear's server at this release. `npm run drift` compares it with Linear's live list, as a maintainer check that needs a read-only Linear key. A tool Linear adds later runs under `access` (allowed at the default) and is not a script method until the plugin classifies it.
- **The default `access` is `all`.** Agents can then create, change and delete Linear items without asking. Set `access` to `"ask-changes"` to ask before every change, or to `"read-only"` to deny them.
- **`"read-only"` is enforced by OpenCode's rules, not by Linear.** The sign-in can write, so an agent without the
  default rules (`/linear-status` names it) could still change Linear. Linear's own read-only server is not used, so
  that changing `access` never needs a new sign-in.
- **Linear's consent page picks the workspace.** The plugin cannot choose a workspace; the sign-in shows Linear's page.
- **Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2 only.** Other releases in `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0` run untested.
- **Linear's rate limits and error text are Linear's.** Linear's MCP server documents no limit of its own; Linear's API
  allows an OAuth app 5,000 requests an hour per user
  ([Rate limiting](https://linear.app/developers/rate-limiting)), which the server's reads presumably count against (not
  verified). One `events_list` call makes up to 8 `list_issues` and 5 `get_notifications` reads.
- **A listing needs no `probe` before it.** `linear.activity`'s account is `<workspace id>/<email>` (the id, because an
  admin can change a workspace's URL key, [workspaces](https://linear.app/docs/workspaces)), which `probe` reads with
  `get_workspace` and `get_user`. A listing that does not know the sign-in yet, after a start of OpenCode or a new
  sign-in, makes the same two reads itself, once, and the plugin keeps the answer in memory for the sign-in; the
  plugin forgets it on every credential update or switch. It then compares its account with that, so Linear signed in
  to another account is still `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH`. If Linear cannot answer those reads the listing is `UNAVAILABLE`. The conformance kit runs on Linear answers
  that are invented, modelled on the tools' descriptions in the live tool list, and not live-verified.
- **A burst bigger than one listing reads is cut, not stopped.** To bound what one call costs, the plugin reads at most
  2,000 assigned issues and 500 notifications per `events_list` call, newest first (8 and 5 pages' worth; Linear's own
  limit is 250 a page, and Linear keeps the history). These caps are the plugin's, not Linear's. In the worst case,
  with ties re-read at the cursor and the pages that show an overflow, one call makes 26 `list_issues` and 17
  `get_notifications` reads, 43 requests against your Linear rate limit (5,000 an hour for an app you sign in to); a
  quiet call makes one of each. Only changes the listing
  has not yet listed count toward them, never ones it re-reads at the cursor's own millisecond. When more of those
  changed after the cursor or `since`, and the page after the caps still holds one, the plugin does not read the
  oldest: the page answers `gap` once (`expired` for a cursor,
  `window-truncated` for `since`) and lists from `gap.since` on, so the next call goes on. The cursor remembers the
  cut until the read has listed what it promised, so changes that arrive meanwhile never cut the read again; only more
  arrivals than one call reads, a new burst, answer a new gap

## [0.0.8] - 2026-11-20

### Added

- **List snapshot** `linear.issues` (`output: "list"`). An app can bind it and render assigned issues without knowing Linear. It calls the existing `linear_issues` read (`list_issues`), not a second client. `linear.activity` stays the events source and is not renamed. No write is declared.

### Fixed

- **`linear.issues` is readable through the tools RPC on every host.** It rides the `issues` method, which declared the model's table as its answer, and OpenCode validates a tools-RPC method's answer against that declaration, so a list read would have been refused `rpc.invalid_output`. The method now declares both shapes, the table and the list. A host test reads the list through the tools RPC on every tested release.
- `linear.issues` leaves out an issue whose identifier, title or workflow state still holds a secret after masking, as every other list source does. It screens the whole text before it cuts, so a secret that straddles the cut cannot pass as a prefix; control characters are dropped, a repeated identifier is listed once, and the 50 items the caps allow stay inside the declared `maxBytes`.

### Changed

- `sources` gains `linear.issues`, so Jelly asks for consent again; `linear.activity` and the `jelly` section are unchanged.
- `linear.issues` checks the account it is asked for against who is signed in, as the events source does: another account is `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH` before any read, and with no account the answer names the signed-in one.
- The list's byte bound is measured in bytes: with 50 maximal multi-byte items it sheds whole items to stay inside the declared `maxBytes`.
- The source-contract devDependency is pinned at v0.3.0, still bundled into `dist/index.js`. Linear declares no fact, hint or routine, so a page reads the same for a consumer still on v0.2.0.

## [0.0.7] - 2026-11-20

### Fixed

- **`events_list` works after any restart of OpenCode, with no `probe` before it.** Until now the plugin kept who is
  signed in only in memory, and only `probe` filled it. A consumer that probes once, at bind, such as Memory, found
  every later listing `UNAVAILABLE` ("no probe has named this sign-in's account") after OpenCode started again, a
  plugin reload, or a second OpenCode process, for good. Now a listing that does not know the sign-in yet makes the two
  identity reads `probe` makes (`get_workspace` and `get_user` with `me`, the declared identity operations, which a
  collection session already allows), once, keeps the answer for the sign-in as `probe` does, and then runs. The
  account check is as strict as before: an account other than the signed-in one is `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH`. When Linear
  cannot answer those reads, or answers in a shape the plugin does not read, the listing is `UNAVAILABLE`, with the
  next step to run `/linear-status` and list again; a refused permission check and a server that cannot be called keep
  their own errors. A request that is invalid, or a cursor for another account, is still refused before any read.
  **For Memory and every consumer:** nothing changes in what the plugin declares or answers when it works; `probe`
  is unchanged. `package.json`'s `sources` is unchanged, so a consumer does not ask to confirm Linear again.

## [0.0.5] - 2026-11-17

### Changed

- The source contract is `@we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract` v0.2.0, pinned as
  `github:we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract#v0.2.0` (commit `88bdc1e`) and bundled into `dist/index.js`, with still
  no runtime dependency. `linear.activity`'s declaration, its pages and `probe`'s answer are unchanged: the plugin
  declares and sends none of the keys v0.2.0 adds, which a consumer still on v0.1.x refuses.
- **The conformance report is complete and ok, with no `noExpiry`.** Linear can lose history a reader has not seen
  (below), so the kit's expired-cursor check and `gap-once-per-read` really run, on a recorded bulk change of 2,100
  issues met by a cursor and by a `since` from before it. Only `failed-holds-cursor` is not applicable, with its reason
  (`atomicPages`): every event comes whole from a page of a list read, and a failed read fails the whole listing. The
  test pins the set of checks that are not applicable, and the recorded Linear now pages by `limit` and cursor as
  Linear does.
- `npm run conformance` (`bun test ./test/conformance`) runs the kit alone and writes
  `reports/conformance-report.json`; `npm run check` still runs it as its `conformance` stage.
- The release kit is revision 4.1 (`1f452e5`, the family's): a release runs `npm run conformance` on the parent in a
  job of its own, with no write token, stops unless the report is `ok` for this version, and attaches it as the Release
  asset `conformance-report.json`, listed in `SHA256SUMS`; the pack job records the kept tarball's sha256 and the stage
  and publish jobs check it after every download. `test/support/jelly-kit.ts` is the family copy that checks jelly's
  `cost` and `admin` lines.
- [In Jelly](docs/jelly.md#tools-and-permissions) carries Jelly's shared rules for every plugin of the family, word for
  word (`scripts/jelly-family-block.md`, which `npm run check` holds it to). The sentence that a tool declared `allow`
  runs what the plugin's own default allows is reworded: a declared `allow` changes nothing in Jelly, and each tool
  follows the access choice and its `readOnly`.
- CI's concurrency group names the event (`ci-<event>-<ref>`), so a run by hand on `master` never cancels the push run
  a release stands on.
- Tested hosts unchanged: OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0 (`TESTED_HOSTS` in `src/constants.ts`), in
  the supported range `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`.

### Fixed

- **A burst of changes bigger than one `events_list` call reads no longer jams the cursor.** Since 0.0.0, more than
  2,000 assigned issues or 500 notifications changed after a cursor answered `TOO_MANY_CHANGES` on every call, so a
  collector could never move on. Those caps are the plugin's own, bounding what one call costs (Linear allows 250 a
  page and keeps the history). Now the oldest changes, past the caps, are cut: the page answers `gap` once,
  `{ reason: "expired", since }` for a cursor or `{ reason: "window-truncated", since }` for `since`, lists from `since`
  on, and its cursor resumes there, so the read drains. Until the read has listed what the gap promised, the cursor
  also carries the newest position the cutting call read (`fi`, `fn`), and changes newer than it get their own
  allowance, so an arrival during the drain never cuts the read again or skips anything after `since`; only more
  arrivals than one call reads, a new burst, answer a new gap. Only items not yet listed count toward the caps, never
  ones at the cursor's own millisecond that the read already listed, and a cut needs the page after the caps to hold
  another such item: a tie the cursor is part way through, or exactly a cap's worth, never answers a gap. A bulk change
  all in one millisecond is cut whole and never read again. `TOO_MANY_CHANGES` is gone. **For Memory and every consumer:** resync on the gap, as the contract
  says; nothing else changes.
- **A late arrival is listed.** A change Linear stamped before the cursor but showed only
